Here is the step-by-step reasoning for each problem:

**[id 10]**
Month 1 downloads: 60
Month 2 downloads: 3 × 60 = 180
Month 3 downloads: 180 - (30% of 180) = 180 - 54 = 126
Total downloads = 60 + 180 + 126 = 366

**[id 11]**
Donuts cost: 3 dozen × $68 = $204
Cupcakes cost: 2 dozen × $80 = $160
Cheesecakes cost: 6 dozen × $55 = $330
Total cost = $204 + $160 + $330 = $694

**[id 12]**
Planting cost: $90
Revenue per year: 7 lemons × $1.50 = $10.50
Maintenance cost per year: $3.00
Net profit per year: $10.50 - $3.00 = $7.50
Years to break even (start earning net positive): $90 / $7.50 = 12 years

**[id 13]**
Let $x$ be the initial number of vacuums.
After selling 1/3, she has (2/3)$x$ left.
After selling 2 more, she has (2/3)$x$ - 2 left.
After selling half of the remainder, she has 1/2 × ((2/3)$x$ - 2) left.
We are told 1/2 × ((2/3)$x$ - 2) = 5
(2/3)$x$ - 2 = 10
(2/3)$x$ = 12
$x$ = 18

**[id 14]**
Total percentage of students must be 100%.
Contemporary: 20%
Jazz: 25%
Hip-hop: 100% - (20% + 25%) = 100% - 45% = 55% 

**[id 15]**
Jewelry profit: $5,000 × 2.5% (0.025) = $125
Electronic gadget profit: $8,000 × 1.2% (0.012) = $96
The maximum profit possible is $125.

**[id 16]**
Distance traveled west = 80 miles
Distance traveled north = 150 miles
Total distance traveled per train = 80 + 150 = 230 miles. 

**[id 17]**
Weekly teacher earnings: 35 hours × $20/hour = $700
Weekly cheerleader coach earnings: 15 hours × $30/hour = $450
Total weekly earnings = $700 + $450 = $1,150
Annual earnings (50 weeks): $1,150 × 50 = $57,500

**[id 18]**
Eggs per day: 3
Days in 4 weeks: 4 × 7 = 28 days
Total eggs eaten: 3 × 28 = 84 eggs
Dozens of eggs eaten: 84 / 12 = 7 dozens

**[id 19]**
Total distance: 12 miles
Desired average speed: 4 mph
Total time allowed: 12 / 4 = 3 hours
First leg: 4 miles in 1 hour
Second leg: 2 miles in 1 hour
Remaining distance to cover: 12 - 4 - 2 = 6 miles
Remaining time allowed: 3 - 1 - 1 = 1 hour
Required speed for the final stretch: 6 miles / 1 hour = 6 mph
